SymbolicEssence.ArchetypalFunction: To embody fear and panic in battle; to paralyze enemies with terror; to be the psychological weapon of war.
SymbolicEssence.SymbolicCore: Fear itself, the panic that breaks armies, terror personified.

CulturalContext.ReligiousOrRitualUse: Invoked to terrify enemies; depicted on war shields; propitiated before battle.
CulturalContext.HistoricalEvolution: Ancient war deity; gave name to phobia; Mars's moon named after him.

SymbolicRepresentation.ImageryNotes: Depicted on shields as terrifying face, lion head, or gorgon; personified as fierce warrior inducing panic.
SymbolicRepresentation.PoeticInvocation: Phobos, terror of the battlefield, whose very presence breaks the courage of armies.
SymbolicRepresentation.DreamForm: A presence that fills you with overwhelming dread, freezing you in place

MetaIntegration.RitualFunction: Shadow work with fear; understanding panic responses; warrior psychology.
AIPromptSeeds: The god whose name became the root of all phobias.
